clue.text: Propose drink then short quiz

parts.note: pop is a fizzy soft drink

indicators.note: short means the word then loses its final letter

parts.note: taken as written before it is cut short
to quiz someone is to question them

explanation.surface: A suitor plans to propose over a drink and then a brief quiz.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims THEN to THE.
explanation.definitionFit: To propose marriage is the idiom for asking the big question of a partner.

clue.text: Additional fish eater has change of heart

indicators.note: the central letter of the word for the animal is swapped for a different one

parts.note: an otter is a river animal that feeds on fish

explanation.surface: An extra fish-eating animal has a sudden change of mind.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle T of OTTER becomes H.
explanation.definitionFit: Other can mean further or extra, as in 'one other thing'.

clue.text: British Olympic champion supports time for sport

indicators.note: in a down clue the champion's name sits below the time letter, holding it up

parts.note: Jessica Ennis(-Hill) won heptathlon gold for Britain at the 2012 London Olympics

explanation.surface: A British gold medallist backs a time slot for her sport.
explanation.walkthrough: Jessica Ennis is a British heptathlete, the 2012 Olympic champion.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennis is a racket game, so it is an example of a sport.

clue.text: Bird tucks into cream daughter put out

indicators.note: the bird's name goes inside the word for the best people

parts.note: the cream of a group is its elite, the best of it
a mina (myna) is an Asian starling
D is the abbreviation for daughter in family trees

explanation.surface: A bird gets into the cream and the daughter is annoyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucks into' looks like eating, but here it means going inside; a mina, also spelt myna, is a talking starling.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone put out of a contest has been knocked out or removed from it.

clue.text: Advocate, for example, game that must undergo revolution

indicators.note: a revolution turns the combined letters right round, so they are read backwards

parts.note: EG is the abbreviation of exempli gratia, for example
RU is rugby union

explanation.surface: Someone champions a game that has to be overhauled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Advocate' looks like a lawyer, but here it is a verb, to push for something.
explanation.definitionFit: To advocate a course of action is to press for it or recommend it.

clue.text: Part of Essex city I found oddly deserted

indicators.note: the letters in odd positions of these words are abandoned, leaving the even ones

explanation.surface: Part of a town in Essex I discovered was strangely empty.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking the 2nd, 4th, 6th... letters of ESSEX CITY I FOUND gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A section is a portion or piece of a whole.

clue.text: Rural girl almost struggles to comprehend English, extraordinary!

indicators.note: to comprehend is to take in, so the shuffled letters hold another letter
the remaining letters struggle into a new order
almost says the last letter of the phrase is dropped

explanation.surface: A country girl, nearly beaten, struggles to understand English: amazing!
explanation.walkthrough: RURAL GIRL less L leaves RURALGIR, which 'struggles' rearranges around E.
explanation.definitionFit: Irregular means out of the ordinary, abnormal, which is what extraordinary says too.

clue.text: Theatre worker on edge composing stirring song

indicators.note: in a down clue the insect sits on top of the border

parts.note: the National is London's National Theatre
a worker ant is the usual crossword worker
a hem is the edge of a garment

explanation.surface: A tense theatre hand is writing a rousing song.
explanation.walkthrough: The National Theatre on London's South Bank is commonly called just 'the National'.
explanation.definitionFit: A country's official hymn is a patriotic, rousing song played at ceremonies.

clue.text: Trained professionals involved in bridge design?

definitions.text: Trained professionals involved in bridge design?

parts.words: Trained professionals involved in bridge design?
parts.note: the bridge is a dental one, a false tooth fixed to its neighbours, not a river crossing

explanation.surface: Qualified experts help to design a bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests civil engineers; a dental bridge replaces missing teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: Specialist dentists fit dental bridges, so they really are involved in designing them.

clue.text: Improving inn with change following refurbishment

indicators.note: the letters are refitted into a new order, as a pub is after a refurbishment

explanation.surface: A pub is improved after a refit brings changes.
explanation.walkthrough: INN and CHANGE together are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Enhancing something means making it better or adding to its quality.

clue.text: Unit of weight around a ton, about right?

indicators.note: about means the letters gathered so far go around another letter

parts.note: CA (circa) means around, as with dates

explanation.surface: A unit of weight comes to roughly a ton: is that about right?
explanation.walkthrough: CA + A + T makes CAAT, which goes 'about' R.
explanation.definitionFit: A carat is a small measure of mass for gemstones, 200 milligrams.

clue.text: Stations Royal Marines on popular island after evacuating there

indicators.note: the marines and the rest come after the emptied word
evacuating empties the word there of its inside letters, keeping just the ends

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable

explanation.surface: Royal Marines are posted on a popular island after the area is evacuated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'evacuating there' leaves TE.
explanation.definitionFit: Termini are end-of-the-line railway or bus stations, the plural of terminus.

clue.text: Spirit and energy required to maintain Kew's top tree

parts.note: gin is a spirit

indicators.note: to maintain is to keep or hold, so the energy word holds a letter inside it

parts.note: go means energy or drive

indicators.note: top means the first letter of Kew's

explanation.surface: Gin and vigour are needed to look after the tree at the top of Kew Gardens.
explanation.walkthrough: Kew Gardens is London's botanic garden; the tree is more often spelt ginkgo.
explanation.definitionFit: The ginkgo or maidenhair is an ancient Chinese species of tree, of which this is a recognised variant spelling.

clue.text: Air-quality device hired if I'm working around university

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go around the letter for the university
working means the letters are put to work in a different order

explanation.surface: An air purifier is hired because I'm busy around the university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' looks like part of the story of the hire, but it signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A humidifier adds moisture to dry room air, a machine improving the atmosphere indoors.

clue.text: Dote on bird pair outside ignored

indicators.note: the two letters on the outside of the bird's name are left off

parts.note: a plover is a wading bird

explanation.surface: Someone dotes on a bird, with the couple outside paying no attention.
explanation.walkthrough: PLOVER loses its outer P and R.
explanation.definitionFit: To dote on someone is to adore them, a strong form of the verb to cherish.

clue.text: Possibly active man said to get mobile phone feature?

parts.note: the active voice is one grammatical voice, so active is an example of a voice

indicators.note: said means the word is heard rather than read, spoken alike to a postal word

parts.note: male means a man

explanation.surface: An energetic man is said to have a feature on his mobile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' marks active as an example of VOICE, as in grammar's active voice.
explanation.definitionFit: Voicemail records callers' messages and is a standard service on a cellphone.

clue.text: Australian organised wild party

indicators.note: organised means the letters are arranged into a fresh order

explanation.surface: An Aussie arranged a riotous party.
explanation.walkthrough: AUSTRALIAN is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman midwinter festival gave its name to any riotous celebration, an orgy of revelry.

clue.text: Where pilots will fly is not yet decided

definitions.meaning: literally aloft in the sky, which is where aviators go
unsettled or uncertain, as an idiom

explanation.surface: Plans for the flight are still uncertain.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both literally aloft and, figuratively, unresolved or uncertain.

clue.text: Capital, is it raised to acquire business in London initially?

indicators.note: to acquire is to take in, so the reversed letters take the initials inside them
in a down clue raised means the words is it are read upwards, backwards
initially means the first letters of these three words

explanation.surface: Is a capital raised to take over a London business?
explanation.walkthrough: IS IT 'raised' gives TISI, which acquires BIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Tbilisi is the capital city of Georgia, in the Caucasus.

clue.text: No idle presence within Airedale region

indicators.note: no means the letters of idle are absent
the letters are present inside the dog's name, so their presence is cancelled

explanation.surface: No lazy dog is to be found inside the Airedale.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove I, D, L, E from AIREDALE in order. An Airedale is a terrier, and Airedale a Yorkshire valley.
explanation.definitionFit: An area is a district or region of land.

clue.text: Remember Thai clutching old lace collar

indicators.note: the words hold the answer tightly inside them, across the gap

explanation.surface: Recall the Thai woman holding an antique lace collar.
explanation.definitionFit: A bertha was a deep lace collar worn on Victorian low-necked dresses.

clue.text: Language coming from council eager for backing

indicators.note: for backing says the hidden letters are read backwards
coming from says the letters are drawn out of the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A language comes from a council keen to support it.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition 'Language coming' is not a phrase meaning the answer; 'coming from' signals the letters come from 'council eager', so the definition is just 'Language'.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaelic is the Celtic tongue of Ireland and the Scottish Highlands.

clue.text: Independent succeeding to bury bill lacking in precision

indicators.note: the word for following buries the bill's letters in its middle

parts.note: next means following or succeeding
AC, account, is a bill

explanation.surface: An independent next in line buries an imprecise bill.
explanation.walkthrough: AC (account) is a standard crossword bill.
explanation.definitionFit: Inexact describes something approximate, not accurate.

clue.text: Father stays away from mad prank

indicators.note: the priest's letters are absent from the word for mad

parts.note: frantic means wild, mad
FR is the abbreviation for Father, a priest

explanation.surface: Father avoids a crazy prank.
explanation.definitionFit: An antic is a silly or playful caper, a piece of foolery.

clue.text: Resistance to wear head-covering seen in swimmer

indicators.note: to wear a cap is to have it around, so the resistance letter goes inside it

parts.note: a cap covers the head
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A swimmer resists wearing a swimming cap.
explanation.walkthrough: The swimmer is a fish, not a person in a bathing cap.
explanation.definitionFit: The carp is a freshwater fish, so in crosswords a swimmer.

clue.text: Look happy if occasionally finding forest giraffe

indicators.note: occasionally means taking every other letter, the second, fourth and so on

explanation.surface: Look cheerful if you come across a forest giraffe.
explanation.walkthrough: Even letters of LOOK HAPPY IF.
explanation.definitionFit: The okapi is a striped Congolese relative of the giraffe living in rainforest.

clue.text: Philosopher tries a lot to be different

indicators.note: the letters are made different by being placed in another order

explanation.surface: A thinker makes a big effort to stand out.
explanation.walkthrough: TRIES A LOT is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Aristotle was the ancient Greek thinker, pupil of Plato.

clue.text: Pomposity of certain MPs shifting position, involving twelve essentially

indicators.note: involving means the shuffled letters take in the core letters
the letters shift into a new order, as politicians shift their stances
essentially means the central letters of twelve

explanation.surface: Twelve MPs' self-importance is shown as they change their stance.
explanation.walkthrough: OF CERTAIN MPS rearranged takes in EL, the core of TWELVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Pomposity is an inflated sense of one's own worth and dignity.
